name: SQL Injection Detection
description: Detection and analysis of SQL injection attempts that may bypass WAF protections.
objective: Determine whether the activity is low-risk scanning, suspicious probing, or malicious exploitation
analysis_steps: Check if the URL contains SQL injection patterns such as quotes, OR conditions, UNION SELECT, comments, or encoded payloads
Check whether the targeted endpoint is sensitive such as /login, /api, /admin, or authentication-related endpoints
Check the user-agent for automation tools such as sqlmap, scripts, curl, python-requests, or unknown user agents
Check the HTTP response status code for possible backend interaction such as 200, 500, or abnormal responses
Check whether the alert indicates repeated attempts or payload variation
Determine whether there is evidence of successful exploitation or data exposure
If enrichment is missing, do not assume that the source IP is malicious

low_risk: Very low number of SQL injection attempts
suspicious: HTTP 200 or 500 response observed but no confirmed exploitation
Repeated attempts or payload variation without confirmed compromise
malicious: High-volume or clearly automated SQL injection attempts
Database error messages or signs of successful query execution
Confirmed data exposure or unauthorized access

suspicious: Review web server and application logs
Check if similar attempts were observed from the same source IP
Perform IP reputation enrichment if needed
Monitor attacker activity for 24 to 48 hours
Escalate if activity increases or exploitation indicators appear
malicious: Block the attacker IP at WAF or firewall level
Update or tune WAF SQL injection rules
Analyze database logs for suspicious queries
Review application logs for exploitation evidence
Escalate to SOC and Incident Response teams
Perform root cause analysis and remediation
